subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Arabica vs. Robusta Markets
description: A quick win: understand Arabica vs. Robusta Markets.

hook.text: Arabica and Robusta aren't just different coffees—they're traded on entirely separate commodity exchanges.

buildup.text: Arabica trades on the ICE exchange in New York. Robusta trades on LIFFE in London. Prices move independently.

discovery.text: Arabica commands higher prices—typically 2–3x Robusta—because it's more delicate and harder to grow.

twist.text: Robusta is increasingly important. It makes up 40% of global output and is essential for espresso blends.

climax.text: Vietnam, the world's Robusta powerhouse, went from no coffee to the #2 global producer in just 30 years.

punchline.text: Two species, two exchanges, two different economies.

details.summary: Arabica and robusta coffees trade on separate exchanges at different price levels. Arabica, prized for flavor, trades on the New York ICE. Robusta, valued for strength and low cost, trades on the London LIFFE. The price gap between them reflects quality differences and market dynamics.
details.whyItMatters: The two-market system creates different economic realities for arabica and robusta farmers, shaping which species whole countries choose to cultivate.
takeaways: Arabica trades on the New York ICE exchange
Robusta trades on the London LIFFE exchange
Arabica typically commands 50 to 100 percent higher prices

faq.question: Why is robusta priced lower than arabica?
faq.answer: Robusta is easier and cheaper to grow, more disease-resistant, and yields more per tree. However, it has a harsher flavor profile with more bitterness. The specialty market overwhelmingly favors arabica, keeping demand and prices for quality arabica higher.

faq.question: Is robusta quality improving?
faq.answer: Yes. Fine robusta is an emerging category, with farmers in Vietnam, India, and Uganda producing carefully processed robusta that rivals mid-grade arabica. The Robusta Quality Program has helped elevate standards and create premium markets for high-quality robusta.
